_README: Industry events / semiconductor conferences that can move watchlist names via product announcements, roadmap disclosures, or competitive read-through. The morning routine (CLAUDE.md) refreshes dates and 'watch' notes via web search each run and adds newly-announced events. 'tickers' = watchlist symbols with direct or read-through exposure. 'partners' = KEY PRIVATE/NON-WATCHLIST COMPANIES whose appearances matter because a holding depends on them (e.g. Ayar Labs is Sivers' flagship CPO customer; Lightmatter is the CPO peer benchmark). ADDED 2026-08-07 after OCP APAC was missed: relevance must be checked against BOTH tickers and partners, and MAJOR EVENT SERIES HAVE REGIONAL EDITIONS (OCP runs Global + APAC + EMEA; SEMICON runs West/Taiwan/Europe/Korea) — enumerate every edition, not just the flagship. 'confidence': confirmed (dates verified) | approx (typical timing, verify) | rumored. Dates ISO YYYY-MM-DD, event-local. Not investment advice.

events.name: SEMICON Taiwan 2026
events.watch: Added 2026-07-30: major Asia-Pacific fab-equipment/WFE show, ~5 days after AI Infra Summit and ~2.5 weeks before ECOC — same September AI-infra/semi catalyst cluster. 2026 program spans 13 themes incl. AI chips, advanced packaging, 3DIC, chiplets, heterogeneous integration; watch for TSMC capacity/pricing commentary and equipment-order read-through. Re-verified 2026-08-04 against SEMI's own release: dates confirmed **Sep 2-4 at Nangang Halls 1 & 2**, with the **conference program running wider than the exhibition — Aug 31 through Sep 4**, so the first TSMC/supply-chain commentary can land two days before the show floor opens. Record scale this year: **1,300+ exhibitors and 4,300+ booths (both all-time highs), 100,000+ attendees from 65 countries.** Named themes now include **silicon photonics** alongside AI chips, advanced packaging and quantum — which makes this a secondary read for the SIVE/SOI optics chain, not only a TSM/GFS event, though ECOC (Sep 20-24) remains the real optics catalyst. 29 days out. **Re-verified 2026-08-06: dates unchanged (Sep 2-4, Nangang) and the OPENING KEYNOTE IS NOW NAMED — Amin Vahdat, SVP & Chief Technologist of AI and Infrastructure at GOOGLE**, on Google's view of AI infrastructure and the semiconductor ecosystem. That is a notable choice for a Taiwanese fab-equipment show: the opening slot goes to a hyperscaler's infrastructure architect rather than to a foundry or WFE executive, which is the demand side setting the agenda for the supply side. Vahdat is also the TPU/networking lineage at Google, so watch for anything on custom-silicon volumes, optics and packaging demand that reads through to TSM/GFS capacity and to the optics chain. Eight named themes this year (advanced manufacturing, heterogeneous integration, compound semiconductors, auto chips, smart manufacturing, sustainability, semiconductor cybersecurity, workforce) — compound semiconductors keeps the secondary InP/photonics read alive. 27 days out. **Re-checked 2026-08-07: dates unchanged (Sep 2-4, Nangang) and the featured-speaker roster has grown beyond the Google/Amin Vahdat opening keynote logged on 08-06 — TSMC is now directly represented, with Dr. Y.J. events.name: CIOE 2026 (China International Optoelectronic Exposition)
events.location: Shenzhen World Exhibition & Convention Center, China
events.watch: **ADDED 2026-08-18 (morning run) — found while checking GlobalFoundries' own events page, which lists GF as participating.** **CIOE runs Sep 9-11, 2026 at the Shenzhen World Exhibition & Convention Center**; dates agree across CIOE's own site, exhibitor listings and trade-fair directories (note the edition number is given inconsistently as the 26th or 27th across sources — the dates are the reliable part). Scale: **4,000+ exhibitors from 30+ countries across eight thematic expos** (information & communication, precision optics, lasers, infrared, UV, sensing, displays/AR-VR, photonics innovation), **co-located with IICIE 2026 and elexcon 2026 for a combined ~320,000 m², 5,000+ exhibitors and 240,000+ visitors.** **Why an optics book should carry a Chinese trade show rather than dismiss it: this is where the Chinese optical-module complex shows its hand, and that complex is currently the live variable in the AAOI thesis.** The FCC draft import ban on Chinese datacenter equipment and optical transceivers (announced Aug 4) is the story that moved AAOI ~20% intraday, and @PhotonCap's 08-11 read is that the ban's *drafting language* — whether it separates company nationality from production origin — decides whether AAOI's competitive relief is real. **CIOE is the venue where the companies on the other side of that rule (Zhongji Innolight, Eoptolink, HG Genuine and peers) exhibit their 800G/1.6T and CPO product lines**, so it is a direct read on how fast the competition is actually moving, independent of the regulatory question. GF's participation adds a silicon-photonics-foundry angle. **Calibrate it: a trade exhibition, not an earnings or standards venue — it produces product-launch and roadmap signal, filtered through a market this book has no primary sources inside, and Western coverage of it is thin and late.** **Nothing here adjudicates a falsifier**; treat as competitive-field intelligence on the pluggable-transceiver layer. Falls between SEMICON Taiwan (Sep 2-4) and ECOC (Sep 20-24) in the September optics run. 22 days out. **Re-checked 2026-08-29 run — now 11 days out and inside the 14-day window for the first time; dates re-confirmed Sep 9-11 at Shenzhen World Exhibition & Convention Center, and the edition ambiguity logged on 08-18 resolves to the 27th (CIOE's own English homepage and the Eventbrite listing both say 27th; the 26th appears only on an older CIOE news page). **The published Information & Communication Expo scope is the sharpening that matters for this book: CIOE itself lists CW lasers, EMLs, VCSELs, silicon-photonics chips, linear driver chips, 1.6T/3.2T modules, CPO/LPO/XPO solutions and advanced packaging/test equipment as showcased categories.** CW lasers and EMLs named as their own category makes this a direct competitive read on the SIVE/SOI layer, not only the pluggable-transceiver layer flagged on 08-18 — it is where the Chinese CW-laser and EML supply shows what it can ship. Named exhibitor detail found this pass: **Accelink** (1.6T and 800G ecosystems plus communication-sensing) and **Luxshare** (CPO, 1.6T modules, LPO/LRO, 1.6T DAC/ACC/AEC, liquid-cooled cold-plate I/O). Tri-show co-location with IICIE 2026 and elexcon 2026 re-confirmed at ~320,000 m2, 5,000+ exhibitors, 240,000+ visitors. **Calibration unchanged and still the honest read: a trade exhibition, product-launch and roadmap signal only, sourced through a market this book has no primary coverage inside — nothing here adjudicates a falsifier.** **Re-verified 2026-09-03 run — 6 days out, inside the 14-day window.** Dates and venue unchanged (Sep 9-11, Shenzhen World Exhibition & Convention Center); note the edition number at source is the **27th** CIOE. The published exhibit scope now names the component layer explicitly — **CW lasers, EMLs, VCSELs, silicon-photonic chips, linear-driver chips, 1.6T/3.2T modules and CPO/LPO/XPO solutions** — which is the most direct statement yet that this show covers the exact layer the SIVE thesis sits in (InP CW DFB), not just finished transceivers. A dedicated seminar on **CPO and OIO** is on the program with ISPs, datacenter equipment vendors and device vendors. Scale re-confirmed at 4,000+ exhibitors from 30+ countries. **Calibration unchanged: this is a Chinese trade exhibition and the read is what domestic CW-laser/EML supply can actually ship — that is a falsifier-adjacent input for SIVE (China closing the CW-laser gap) but a trade-show claim is not evidence of qualified volume, and nothing here adjudicates a falsifier.**

events.name: AI Infra Summit 2026
events.watch: Speaker list expanded to 400+ as of 2026-07-27 scan (8,000+ attendees, 300+ sessions, 8 stages) across 5 tracks: Compute, Data Movement, Physical AI, Data & Models, AI Data Center. Named speakers now include Lip-Bu Tan (CEO, Intel) and Dave Lazovsky (EVP, Marvell) on the main stage, plus Jeff Dean (Google), Kripa Krishnan (VP, Meta AI Infrastructure) — direct read-through for INTC and MRVL specifically, not just the thematic complex, alongside NVDA/AVGO/WULF/META exposure already logged. Falls 5 days before ECOC 2026, inside the same September AI-infra catalyst window. **Re-verified 2026-08-17 end-of-day run at source (ai-infra-summit.com) — dates and venue confirmed (Sep 15-17, Santa Clara Convention Center), and the speaker roster has resolved further since the 07-27 scan.** **Newly named and directly watchlist-relevant: Ian Buck (NVIDIA, VP Hyperscale & HPC Computing)** — the CUDA lineage and the person who speaks for NVIDIA's hyperscale business rather than its product marketing — **and Santosh Janardhan (Meta, Head of Infrastructure)**, plus Monique Picou (Google, Chief Product Supply Officer, a supply-chain rather than an engineering voice). **Lip-Bu Tan (CEO, Intel) is re-confirmed on the main stage.** **Marvell and Broadcom are both listed as Platinum Partner sponsors** — carried as sponsorship, not as confirmed speaking slots; the Dave Lazovsky (EVP, Marvell) main-stage listing logged on 07-27 was not visible on the page read this pass and is not re-asserted here. Structure unchanged: five tracks (AI Data Centers, Compute, Data Movement, Data & Models, Physical AI), eight stages, 400+ speakers. No neocloud or energy-infrastructure speaker is visible in the main lineup, so the **WULF read-through on this entry remains thematic rather than evidenced**. Falls 5 days before ECOC, inside the same September AI-infra catalyst window. 29 days out. **Re-verified 2026-08-18 morning run at source — dates and venue confirmed (Sep 15-17, Santa Clara Convention Center), and the keynote roster resolved into named executives this pass.** Confirmed speakers: **Lip-Bu Tan (CEO, Intel — a watchlist company, and the only watchlist CEO on the program)**, **Ian Buck (VP Hyperscale & HPC Computing, NVIDIA)**, Peter DeSantis (SVP Foundational AI Models, Amazon), Monique Picou (Chief Product Supply Officer, Google), Santosh Janardhan (Head of Infrastructure, Meta — watchlist), Karan Batta (SVP Oracle Cloud Infrastructure), and Sachin Katti (VP Compute Strategy & GPT-Infra, OpenAI), with AMD, Qualcomm and Dell also represented. Scale confirmed at 8,000+ attendees, 400 speakers, 250 partners, eight stages. **Two things this changes for the entry: Intel's CEO speaking makes INTC's presence direct rather than thematic (this is a strategy venue, not a product launch — expect foundry/AI-accelerator positioning, and note Crescent Island is being presented at Hot Chips three weeks earlier), and Meta's head of infrastructure appearing here alongside Meta's networking keynote at Hot Interconnects (Aug 19-21) means the same operator describes its own constraints twice inside a month.** **The WULF read-through on this entry remains thematic rather than evidenced — still no neocloud or energy-infrastructure speaker visible in the lineup.** Falls 5 days before ECOC, inside the same September AI-infra catalyst window. 28 days out. **Re-verified 2026-09-01 (week's first run) at source and via trade coverage — dates and venue unchanged (Sep 15-17, Santa Clara Convention Center), 14 days out and inside the alert window.** Two changes since the 08-18 pass. **(1) The Dave Lazovsky (Marvell) main-stage slot, which was logged on 07-27 and then NOT re-asserted on 08-18 because it had dropped off the page, is back and specified: Lazovsky is listed delivering a keynote on AI inference at scale.** That restores MRVL from sponsor-only to a named speaking slot, and 'inference at scale' is the framing that bears on the custom-XPU/attach-rate question the MRVL thesis tracks. **(2) Jeff Dean (Chief Scientist and Technical Lead, Gemini, Google) is confirmed on the Main Stage**, alongside Lip-Bu Tan (CEO, Intel), Ian Buck (VP & GM Hyperscale and HPC, NVIDIA), Peter DeSantis (Amazon), Monique Picou (Google), Sachin Katti (OpenAI) and Santosh Janardhan (Meta) — all re-confirmed. Program is now described as **six streams** (Main Stage, Data & Models, Compute, Data Movement, AI Data Center, Physical AI), up from the five logged previously; 8,000+ attendees unchanged. **The WULF read-through is still thematic, not evidenced — no neocloud or energy-infrastructure speaker is visible in the lineup.** Nothing here adjudicates a falsifier.

events.name: ECOC 2026 (European Conference on Optical Communication)
events.watch: THE optics event for the small-caps: CPO (co-packaged optics), 800G/1.6T transceivers, EML/DFB laser and InP-substrate progress. Direct catalyst window for Sivers (CPO lasers) and Soitec (photonics substrates); DSP/optics read-through for MRVL & AVGO. Lumentum/Coherent disclosures here reset the whole InP supply picture.

events.name: GlobalFoundries Technology Summit (GTS) 2026 — China
events.watch: **ADDED 2026-09-03 (promoted from the GTS North America entry, whose Sep 2 date has now passed and which was removed this run).** GF's flagship customer/partner technology summit runs as a regional series; per the README's regional-edition rule the remaining 2026 editions each get their own entry as they come inside the 30-day window. **Dates re-verified this run against GF's own GTS page: Shanghai Sep 22, Hsinchu Sep 24, Munich Oct 15.** Format is GF and industry-leader keynotes plus deep dives into GF's differentiated process platforms (RF-SOI, silicon photonics, FD-SOI, automotive/power) and customer/ecosystem results. **Why it matters for GFS: this is where the specialty-foundry case acquires roadmap and design-win evidence bearing on the drivers "specialty mix defends pricing vs commodity nodes" and "silicon photonics becomes a real revenue line as CPO scales" — it does NOT bear on the pricing-war or utilisation falsifiers.** Secondary read: GF is named in the SIVE thesis as an ecosystem partner (GlobalFoundries reference designs for hyperscalers incl. AMD), so any silicon-photonics platform announcement is a read-through into the CPO chain. **Calibrate honestly: a customer/partner technology event, not an investor day — expect platform and partnership announcements, not guidance, and no session-level agenda is published at source for these editions as of this pass. Nothing here adjudicates a falsifier.** **Regional angle specific to this edition: it lands in the Asian supply chain days after SEMICON Taiwan (Sep 2-4) and CIOE (Sep 9-11), so any GF photonics platform news here can be cross-read against what those two shows produce.** 19 days out.

events.name: Marvell Technology Investor Day 2026
events.location: New York City (in-person by invitation; live webcast)
events.watch: **ADDED 2026-08-18 (morning run) — a real calendar gap: a watchlist company has a confirmed, dated, WEBCAST management event and this calendar did not carry it.** **Marvell announced on 2026-08-03, in the same release that set its Q2 FY2027 earnings call, that it will hold an Investor Day on the morning of Tue Oct 6, 2026 in New York City, with Chairman and CEO Matt Murphy and the senior leadership team presenting.** In-person attendance is by invitation only, but **the event is webcast live via the Events section of investor.marvell.com** — which is what separates this from the broker conferences elsewhere on this calendar: it is a company-controlled disclosure venue with a public feed, not a 1x1 program. It sat unlogged for fifteen days. **Why it matters for this book specifically: an investor day is where multi-year financial targets and segment models get set, and MRVL is the one watchlist name whose thesis turns on a disclosure of exactly that kind.** The MRVL falsifiers are "loss/insourcing of a flagship custom program", "CPO disintermediates pluggable DSPs faster than Marvell adapts", and a shift in data-center guide language — all three are TAM-and-roadmap claims that an investor day either substantiates with a model or conspicuously does not. **Sequencing is the other reason to carry it: the Q2 FY2027 print lands Thu Aug 27 at 1:45pm PT, five and a half weeks BEFORE this event**, so the quarter sets the near-term facts and the investor day sets the multi-year frame on top of them. Note the tape context this is being scheduled into: **UBS cut its MRVL target 340 → 300 on 2026-08-17**, and the name has run 74 → 316 and back inside six months. **Nothing here adjudicates a falsifier yet — it is a scheduled opportunity for one to be adjudicated.** 49 days out; outside the 30-day window, carried so it is not missed again.
